# Create, view, and print your family tree for free!

 Bring your ancestors' history to life:  
**create your family tree online for free**  
 and share it with your family! 

[Create my family tree](https://en.geneanet.org/create-your-family-tree/)

![Image 1](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/build_tree_landing_gw.png)

## Your online genealogy software

Easily build your family tree online using an intuitive and powerful interface: add branches, link historical documents, and enrich your family history. Automatically find hints about your ancestors, and share your research with your close ones.

*   Free and unlimited family tree
*   Backup, restore, and sharing tools
*   Automatic detection of inconsistencies
*   And much more!

![Image 2](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/visualize_tree_landing_gw.png)

## View your family tree in a new way

Bring your genealogy research to life! Geneanet turns your raw data into clear visual displays to help you understand the journey of your ancestors.

*   Map of ancestors by lineage
*   Customized historical timeline
*   Illustrated statistics (last names, first names, occupations, average ages, etc.)

![Image 3](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/treeprint_landing_gw.png)

## Print your family tree

Customize your family tree and instantly download a printable PDF version. Whether you're printing it quickly at home or having it professionally printed, bring your research to life on a long-lasting paper copy.

*   Wide range of family tree templates
*   Advanced customization (colors, display of last names, first names, dates, etc.)
*   Download as a PDF for printing at home or at a print shop

![Image 4](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/bookprint_landing_gw.png)

## Create your genealogy book

Turn your research into a real family book with our automatic publishing tools. In just a few clicks, compile information about your ancestors, their biographies, and your photos to create an organized family chronicle, ready to be shared and passed on to future generations.

*   Book of ancestry or descent spanning several generations
*   Advanced customization (language, format of ages, cover title, etc.)
*   Book available for download in PDF format or by mail order

 More than 2.5 million family trees already created 

Without Geneanet, I would never have been able to build my family tree and my wife's one. A big thank you for this great work and for this very user-friendly tool!

Walter Gotre (sebastian55)

Thanks to Geneanet, I've been able to really grow my family tree. The most surprising thing is that it turns out my father and mother share the same ancestor. It's truly incredible. (Well, in small villages, it's not that rare, of course, since the community was small and people married within it.) But it was still nice to discover that. My parents are sadly no longer with us, but they were still alive when I found this out. They were completely stunned.

## Frequently Asked Questions

*    How many generations back can I trace my family tree?   Our online genealogy tool is designed to support an unlimited number of generations. Unlike other services, we don't restrict the size of your family tree: whether you go back 5, 20, or 50 generations, Geneanet hosts all of your findings for free.  
*    Can I import an existing family tree?   Yes, thanks to the international GEDCOM standard (GEnealogical Data COMmunication). If you've already started your research using another software or website, you don't need to type it all over again: just export your family tree in .ged format and import it into Geneanet.  
*    Can I import photos and documents into my family tree?   Yes, absolutely. In genealogy, images are invaluable sources: family photos, old postcards, photos of graves, and digitized archives tell the story of our ancestors. On Geneanet, you can directly import your own photos and documents or attach resources already available on the site to your family tree: photos of graves, postcards, records, or archives shared by other members. If you import your family tree from a genealogy software program, you can use our [Geneanet Upload](https://en.geneanet.org/product/upload) tool to automatically upload your photos along with your GEDCOM file.  
*    Can I share my family tree with my family?   Yes, sharing and collaboration are core values at Geneanet. We've designed simple features that let you share your discoveries with your close ones while keeping total control over your data. Invite your family members via email to view your family tree and assign them the status of visitor if they're just curious, or the status of admin if they want to help you complete some branches or add family photos.

# Create, view, and print your family tree for free!

 Bring your ancestors' history to life:  
**create your family tree online for free**  
 and share it with your family! 

[Create my family tree](https://en.geneanet.org/create-your-family-tree/)

![Image 1](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/build_tree_landing_gw.png)

## Your online genealogy software

Easily build your family tree online using an intuitive and powerful interface: add branches, link historical documents, and enrich your family history. Automatically find hints about your ancestors, and share your research with your close ones.

*   Free and unlimited family tree
*   Backup, restore, and sharing tools
*   Automatic detection of inconsistencies
*   And much more!

![Image 2](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/visualize_tree_landing_gw.png)

## View your family tree in a new way

Bring your genealogy research to life! Geneanet turns your raw data into clear visual displays to help you understand the journey of your ancestors.

*   Map of ancestors by lineage
*   Customized historical timeline
*   Illustrated statistics (last names, first names, occupations, average ages, etc.)

![Image 3](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/treeprint_landing_gw.png)

## Print your family tree

Customize your family tree and instantly download a printable PDF version. Whether you're printing it quickly at home or having it professionally printed, bring your research to life on a long-lasting paper copy.

*   Wide range of family tree templates
*   Advanced customization (colors, display of last names, first names, dates, etc.)
*   Download as a PDF for printing at home or at a print shop

![Image 4](https://geneacdn.net/bundles/geneanetgeneweb/images/landing/bookprint_landing_gw.png)

## Create your genealogy book

Turn your research into a real family book with our automatic publishing tools. In just a few clicks, compile information about your ancestors, their biographies, and your photos to create an organized family chronicle, ready to be shared and passed on to future generations.

*   Book of ancestry or descent spanning several generations
*   Advanced customization (language, format of ages, cover title, etc.)
*   Book available for download in PDF format or by mail order

 More than 2.5 million family trees already created

My parents are sadly no longer with us, but they were still alive when I found this out. They were completely stunned.

## Frequently Asked Questions

*    How many generations back can I trace my family tree?   Our online genealogy tool is designed to support an unlimited number of generations. Unlike other services, we don't restrict the size of your family tree: whether you go back 5, 20, or 50 generations, Geneanet hosts all of your findings for free.  
*    Can I import an existing family tree?   Yes, thanks to the international GEDCOM standard (GEnealogical Data COMmunication). If you've already started your research using another software or website, you don't need to type it all over again: just export your family tree in .ged format and import it into Geneanet.  
*    Can I import photos and documents into my family tree?   Yes, absolutely. In genealogy, images are invaluable sources: family photos, old postcards, photos of graves, and digitized archives tell the story of our ancestors. On Geneanet, you can directly import your own photos and documents or attach resources already available on the site to your family tree: photos of graves, postcards, records, or archives shared by other members. If you import your family tree from a genealogy software program, you can use our [Geneanet Upload](https://en.geneanet.org/product/upload) tool to automatically upload your photos along with your GEDCOM file.  
*    Can I share my family tree with my family?   Yes, sharing and collaboration are core values at Geneanet. We've designed simple features that let you share your discoveries with your close ones while keeping total control over your data. Invite your family members via email to view your family tree and assign them the status of visitor if they're just curious, or the status of admin if they want to help you complete some branches or add family photos.

## Brief Life History of Gerritje Van

When Gerritje Van de Pol was born on 1 June 1852, in Ede, Gelderland, Netherlands, her father, Evert van de Pol, was 58 and her mother, Rikje Hogeweg, was 28. She married Johannes Albertus Vink on 14 December 1878, in Ede, Gelderland, Netherlands. They were the parents of at least 4 sons and 3 daughters. She died on 28 January 1887, in her hometown, at the age of 34.

## Biography

Evert was born in 1793. Baptised on 22 May 1793 in Lunteren, Gelderland, Nederland.

**First marriage**: Evert van de Pol married Maria van Davelaar on 13 Feb 1830. in Ede, Gelderland, Nederland. [[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Van%20de%20Pol-188#_note-BSHu16005)

**Second marriage**: Evert van de Pol married Rikje Hogeweg on 11 May 1844 in Ede, Gelderland, Nederland. [[2]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Van%20de%20Pol-188#_note-BSHu14847)

He passed away on 30 Aug 1853 in Ede, Gelderland, Nederland. [[3]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Van%20de%20Pol-188#_note-BSOv85968)

Profile entered [[4]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Van%20de%20Pol-188#_note-0)

## Biography

Evert was born in 1793. Baptised on 22 May 1793 in Lunteren, Gelderland, Nederland.

**First marriage**: Evert van de Pol married Maria van Davelaar on 13 Feb 1830. in Ede, Gelderland, Nederland. [[1]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Van%20de%20Pol-188#_note-BSHu16005)

**Second marriage**: Evert van de Pol married Rikje Hogeweg on 11 May 1844 in Ede, Gelderland, Nederland. [[2]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Van%20de%20Pol-188#_note-BSHu14847)

He passed away on 30 Aug 1853 in Ede, Gelderland, Nederland. [[3]](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Van%20de%20Pol-188#_note-BSOv85968)
